items.name: Ahmad Zahid Hamidi
items.role: UMNO President (since 2018) / Barisan Nasional Chairman / Deputy Prime Minister & Minister of Rural and Regional Development (since Dec 2022)
items.profile: UMNO's crisis-survival president who rebuilt BN from its 2018 nadir into the south's dominant force by 2026, but remains permanently shadowed by corruption litigation and internal opposition to his leadership style.

items.name: Mohammad Najib Abdul Razak
items.role: Former Prime Minister (2009-2018) / former UMNO President & BN Chairman — imprisoned, legacy influence on UMNO base
items.profile: Malaysia's only convicted former PM, whose 1MDB scandal toppled BN in 2018 but whose 'Bossku' persona still mobilizes UMNO's rural base — a live question for GE16 as his release campaign resonates within the party.

items.name: Mohamad Hasan (Tok Mat)
items.role: UMNO Deputy President / BN Deputy Chairman / Minister of Foreign Affairs (since Dec 2023)
items.seat: P.132 Rembau; Rantau (Negeri Sembilan state seat)
items.profile: UMNO's most electorally successful state leader of the 2000s and now Foreign Minister; the deputy president whose quiet competence is widely seen as the party's safest face for a solo GE16 campaign.

items.name: Ismail Sabri Yaakob
items.role: Former Prime Minister (Aug 2021-Nov 2022) / Bera UMNO division chief
items.profile: The accidental ninth PM who inherited a collapsing coalition, survived a year of crisis government, and now watches BN's 2026 resurgence from the backbench as a potential elder statesman.

items.name: Khairy Jamaluddin
items.role: Former UMNO Youth chief & Minister — expelled from UMNO (Jan 2023); now broadcaster/podcast host (Keluar Sekejap, Hot FM)
items.seat: P.132 Rembau (2008-2022); contested P.107 Sungai Buloh in 2022 (lost)
items.profile: UMNO's lost modernizer — expelled after challenging Zahid, he has become Malaysia's most influential political podcaster and the unofficial standard-bearer of the anti-Zahid faction ahead of GE16.

items.name: Hishammuddin Hussein
items.role: Former Senior Minister & Defence Minister — senior UMNO elder, sidelined from current leadership
items.seat: P.153 Sembrong (2004-2022; did not contest GE15)
items.profile: Third-generation UMNO royalty who held every top security portfolio, now a senior elder watching his nephew Onn Hafiz carry the family's political future in Johor.

items.name: Tengku Zafrul Aziz
items.role: Former UMNO Supreme Council member & Minister — left UMNO for PKR (May 2025); now Senior Political Advisor to the PM (since Mar 2026)
items.seat: None (Senator 2020-2022, 2023-2025; lost P.096 Kuala Selangor in GE15)
items.profile: The banker-minister who jumped from UMNO to PKR in 2025 — a symbol of BN's technocratic drain and of Anwar's poaching of BN talent, now advising the PM from inside PH.

items.name: Azalina Othman Said
items.role: UMNO Vice-President / Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law & Institutional Reform, since Dec 2022)
items.profile: UMNO's most senior woman — a trailblazing lawyer-politician running law and institutional reform for the unity government while anchoring BN's legal defence narrative.

items.name: Johari Abdul Ghani
items.role: UMNO Vice-President / BN Treasurer-General / Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry (since Dec 2025)
items.seat: P.119 Titiwangsa (the only BN MP in Klang Valley)
items.profile: UMNO's accountant-in-chief and Klang Valley's only BN MP — the party's urban professional face, now running investment policy as PH-BN federal cooperation deepens.

items.name: Mohamed Khaled Nordin
items.role: UMNO Vice-President / Minister of Defence (since Dec 2023)
items.profile: The former Johor MB and now Defence Minister — a tested administrator whose seniority gives UMNO real cabinet weight in the unity government.

items.name: Ahmad Maslan
items.role: UMNO Johor Deputy Chairman / Pontian division chief / Deputy Minister of Works (since Dec 2023)
items.profile: UMNO's veteran fixer and former secretary-general — the party's administrative backbone in Johor and a dependable federal deputy minister.

items.name: Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki
items.role: UMNO Secretary-General (since Mar 2023) / MARA Chairman (since Mar 2023)
items.profile: The religious-affairs technocrat who beat Khairy for UMNO Youth and now runs the party as secretary-general — Zahid's organizational anchor and public attack-dog.

items.name: Muhamad Akmal Saleh
items.role: UMNO Youth Chief (15th, since Mar 2023) / Jasin UMNO division chief
items.profile: UMNO Youth's combative young doctor — a social-media-savvy Malay-rights firebrand whose controversies both energise the base and alarm BN's non-Malay allies.

items.name: Noraini Ahmad
items.role: UMNO Wanita Chief (since Jun 2018) / Minister of Plantation and Commodities (since Dec 2025)
items.profile: UMNO's Wanita chief and a cabinet minister who has bounced back from demotion to full minister — the party's main channel to female and commodity-sector voters.

items.name: Onn Hafiz Ghazi
items.role: 19th Menteri Besar of Johor (since Mar 2022) / Johor UMNO Chairman (since 2023) / Johor BN Chairman (since 2024)
items.profile: The 47-year-old Johor MB who delivered BN's biggest 2026 victory — dynastic heir of the Onn-Hussein line and the strongest argument that BN can win alone.

items.name: Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail
items.role: 14th Menteri Besar of Pahang (since May 2018) / UMNO Vice-President (since Mar 2023) / Pahang UMNO Chairman
items.profile: The quietly effective Pahang MB who held BN's rural heartland through the 2018 and 2022 storms and now sits in UMNO's top leadership.

items.name: Saarani Mohamad
items.role: 13th Menteri Besar of Perak (since Dec 2020) / Perak UMNO & BN Chairman
items.profile: The teacher-turned-MB who has kept Perak stable under a BN-PH arrangement — living proof of BN's split personality between federal cooperation and solo ambitions.

items.name: Ab Rauf Yusoh
items.role: 13th Chief Minister of Melaka (since Mar 2023) / Melaka UMNO & BN Chairman (since Jul 2018)
items.profile: Melaka's BN chairman-CM steering the state toward possible BN-PN cooperation — a bellwether for whether the pact spreads ahead of GE16.

items.name: Ismail Lasim
items.role: 9th/12th Menteri Besar of Negeri Sembilan (since Aug 2026) / N9 UMNO deputy chairman & information chief / Kuala Pilah division chief
items.seat: Senaling (Negeri Sembilan state seat; also Juasseh 2018-2023)
items.profile: The veteran Tok Mat lieutenant who reclaimed Negeri Sembilan for BN in 2026 — the fresh face of BN's southern resurgence at state level.

items.name: Bung Moktar Radin
items.role: Former Sabah UMNO & BN Chairman (2018-2025) / former Sabah Deputy CM I (2020-2023) — died in office 5 Dec 2025, legacy influence
items.seat: P.187 Kinabatangan (1999 until death, Dec 2025); Lamag (Sabah state seat)
items.profile: The gruff Kinabatangan boss who held Sabah UMNO together through defeat and coalition rupture; his 2025 death removed BN's most formidable Sabah operator on the eve of GE16.

items.name: Noh Omar
items.role: Former Minister & Selangor UMNO/BN chairman — left UMNO for Bersatu (joined Jan 2025); now Bersatu Supreme Council member
items.profile: The former Selangor UMNO boss who jumped to Bersatu in 2025 — emblematic of the Malay-old-guard outflow from BN into PN as GE16 approaches.

items.name: Annuar Musa
items.role: Former BN Secretary-General & Minister — expelled from UMNO (Dec 2022); joined PAS (Mar 2023); now PAS Central Working Committee member
items.profile: UMNO's eloquent strategist turned PAS stalwart — the highest-profile UMNO defector to the Islamist camp, now relevant again as BN-PN pacts bloom.

items.name: Shahrir Abdul Samad
items.role: Former Johor MB & Minister / former BN Backbenchers Club chairman — UMNO elder statesman
items.profile: The former Johor MB and veteran parliamentarian who embodies UMNO's parliamentary-establishment tradition — a voice of continuity as the party picks a GE16 course.

items.name: Wee Ka Siong
items.role: 11th MCA President (since Nov 2018) / Ayer Hitam MP
items.profile: MCA's survivalist president who has kept the party's two federal seats through two brutal elections — now betting on BN's resurgence while fighting for a larger Chinese voice in a Malay-first coalition.

items.name: Liow Tiong Lai
items.role: 10th MCA President (2013-2018) / former Minister — MCA elder statesman
items.profile: The former health and transport minister who led MCA through its GE13-GE14 collapse — an elder voice on how MCA must rebuild its Chinese support.

items.name: Wee Jeck Seng
items.role: MCA Vice-President (since Sep 2023) / Tanjung Piai MP / KTMB Chairman-designate
items.profile: MCA's by-election hero and Tanjung Piai incumbent — one of only two MCA MPs, holding the party's southern beachhead inside BN's Johor stronghold.

items.name: Chong Sin Woon
items.role: MCA Secretary-General (since Sep 2019)
items.profile: MCA's secretary-general and former education deputy minister — the party's chief organiser as it tries to convert BN's 2026 Malay resurgence into Chinese support.

items.name: Lim Ban Hong
items.role: MCA Vice-President (since Nov 2018) / Melaka MCA Chairman / Kelebang state assemblyman
items.profile: MCA's Melaka chief and trade-deputy-minister veteran — the party's state-level anchor in a Melaka election that could be the next BN-PN test.

items.name: Ti Lian Ker
items.role: MCA Kuantan division chief / former MCA Vice-President (2018-2023) / former Senator (2018-2024)
items.profile: MCA's interfaith advocate and former national-unity deputy minister — the party's bridge to Buddhist and non-Malay religious constituencies.

items.name: Yew Teong Look
items.role: Former MCA Vice-President (2018-2023) / former Wangsa Maju MP — MCA elder
items.profile: A veteran MCA federal figure from the pre-2008 era — part of the party's institutional memory as it contests for relevance.

items.name: Michael Chong
items.role: Long-serving Chairman of MCA Public Services & Complaints Department / MCA central committee figure
items.seat: None (party functionary and public face, not an elected MP)
items.profile: The face of MCA's complaints bureau — a media-perennial whose community-service profile is the party's most direct link to ordinary Chinese voters.

items.name: S. Sivasubramaniam
items.role: 11th MIC President (since Jul 2024)
items.seat: None (contested P.062 Sungai Siput in GE15, lost)
items.profile: MIC's president since 2024, tasked with reviving a party reduced to one MP — his challenge is converting BN's Malay resurgence into Indian-community support at GE16.

items.name: S. Vigneswaran
items.role: 10th MIC President (2018-2024) / PM's Special Envoy to South Asia (since Nov 2021)
items.profile: The former Senate president who ran MIC through its 2018-2024 wilderness — now the party's elder, still holding a federal envoy post.

items.name: M. Saravanan
items.role: MIC Deputy President / Tapah MP — MIC's sole federal MP
items.profile: MIC's only MP and former human-resources minister — the party's most experienced federal operator, now number two under Sivasubramaniam.

items.name: Subramaniam Sathasivam (Dr S. Subramaniam)
items.role: 9th MIC President (2013-2018) / former Minister — MIC elder statesman
items.profile: The doctor-politician who led MIC through its last years of federal power — a respected elder whose 2018 defeat closed MIC's era of ministerial influence.

items.name: M. Asojan (Asojan Muniyandy)
items.role: MIC Johor Chairman (since Nov 2016) / former Gambir state assemblyman
items.profile: MIC's Johor boss, whose grassroots machinery rode BN's 2026 Johor landslide — a state-level operator who matters for MIC's GE16 seat claims in the south.

items.name: Arthur Joseph Kurup
items.role: 2nd PBRS President (since Jan 2023) / Sabah BN Chairman (since Jan 2026) / Minister of Natural Resources & Environmental Sustainability (since Dec 2025)
items.seat: P.182 Pensiangan; Sook (Sabah state seat, since Nov 2025)
items.profile: The young PBRS president who inherited his father's party and has been fast-tracked to cabinet — Sabah BN's new chairman as it tries to rebuild after Bung Moktar's death.

items.name: Abang Abdul Rahman Zohari Abang Openg
items.role: Premier of Sarawak / GPS Chairman / PBB President
items.profile: Sarawak's longest-effective premier; GPS's undisputed leader who has converted Sarawak autonomy into a federal bargaining chip, keeping 23 seats safe for the unity government's majority.

items.name: Fadillah Haji Yusof
items.role: Deputy Prime Minister II / GPS (PBB) / Energy Transition Minister
items.profile: Sarawak's man in Putrajaya — DPM II and GPS's federal anchor, balancing MA63 advocacy with loyalty to the unity government.

items.name: Stephen Rundi Utom
items.role: Sarawak Deputy Premier II / PBB vice-president
items.profile: Long-serving PBB state minister and one of Abang Johari's two deputy premiers; utilities and food-security portfolio holder.

items.name: Douglas Uggah Embas
items.role: Sarawak Deputy Premier I / PBB deputy president
items.profile: PBB's number two and the lead negotiator on MA63; the man who sets Sarawak's deadlines with the federal government.

items.name: Alexander Nanta Linggi
items.role: GPS Sec-Gen / PBB Supreme Council
items.profile: GPS secretary-general and Works Minister; Kapit's long-serving MP representing the upper Rajang.

items.name: James Jemut Masing
items.role: PRS President / former Sarawak Deputy Chief Minister (deceased 2021 — legacy)
items.profile: Founding PRS president and iconic Iban leader; his legacy dominates Baleh and rural Sarawak politics.

items.name: Joseph Salang Gandum
items.role: PRS deputy president / former federal minister
items.profile: Veteran PRS leader and Iban federal voice from Lubok Antu, straddling the Sarawak-Kalimantan borderlands.

items.name: Richard Riot Jaem
items.role: SUPP advisor / former federal minister
items.profile: Long-serving SUPP federal minister who represented Serian for three decades, bridging Dayak and Chinese constituencies.

items.name: Sim Kui Hian
items.role: SUPP president / Sarawak Deputy Premier III
items.profile: SUPP president and third deputy premier; the Chinese vote's anchor in Sarawak's GPS.

items.name: Tiong King Sing
items.role: PDP president / federal minister
items.profile: Wealthy Bintulu tycoon-politician leading PDP; tourism minister whose business network anchors GPS's economic wing.

items.name: Hajiji Noor
items.role: Sabah Chief Minister / GRS Chairman / GAGASAN President
items.profile: Sabah's chief minister steering GRS through a fragile coalition with PH while managing the WARISAN surge of 2025.

items.name: Maximus Ongkili
items.role: PBS President / former federal minister
items.profile: PBS's veteran Kadazan-Dusun leader; the conscience voice for non-Muslim Bumiputera interests inside GRS.

items.name: Jeffrey Kitingan
items.role: STAR President / Sabah Deputy Chief Minister I
items.profile: Veteran Kadazan-Dusun rights campaigner and Harvard-educated DCM; the ideological heart of GRS's MA63 push.

items.name: Ewon Benedick
items.role: UPKO President / federal minister (PH-aligned, Sabah)
items.profile: Young Kadazan-Dusun minister who took UPKO fully into PH — a key PH beachhead in Sabah.

items.name: Shafie Apdal
items.role: WARISAN President / former Sabah Chief Minister
items.profile: WARISAN's founder-leader; 2025 DUN surge re-established him as Sabah's leading opposition figure.

items.name: Junz Wong
items.role: WARISAN deputy president / former Sabah minister
items.profile: WARISAN's deputy and Sandakan-base leader; young corporate-professional face of the party.

items.name: Jannie Lasimbang
items.role: WARISAN vice-president / former MP
items.profile: Rights lawyer and former Papar MP; WARISAN's voice on indigenous and human-rights issues.

items.name: Peter Anthony
items.role: KDM President / former Sabah minister
items.profile: Controversial KDM founder whose forgery conviction complicates his seat's status; represents Kadazan-Dusun welfare politics.

items.name: Zuraida Kamaruddin
items.role: PBM President / former federal minister
items.profile: Serial defector who ended up founding PBM; her Ampang loss marked the end of her front-rank career.

items.name: Maszlee Malik
items.role: Independent / former Education Minister (originally PKR, then independent)
items.profile: Former education minister returned to Parliament as an independent in the 2024 Pulai by-election — a wildcard in Johor.

items.name: Khalid Samad
items.role: Independent / former Federal Territories Minister (ex-AMANAH)
items.profile: Veteran progressive-Islamist figure now outside party politics; occasional commentator on unity-government issues.

items.name: Anwar Ibrahim
items.role: 10th Prime Minister of Malaysia; Minister of Finance; President of PKR; Chairman of Pakatan Harapan
items.profile: Malaysia's longest-running reformist leader and current PM; the anchor of PH and the Unity Government, whose GE16 fortunes depend on PKR's squeezed Malay base and the Bersama splinter.

items.name: Wan Azizah Wan Ismail
items.role: PKR founding president & party advisor; former Deputy Prime Minister (2018–2020); MP Bandar Tun Razak; spouse of PM Anwar
items.profile: The matriarch of Reformasi who founded PKR and broke gender barriers at the highest levels; remains a symbolic anchor of PKR's founding generation.

items.name: Nurul Izzah Anwar
items.role: Deputy President of PKR (2025–); MP Pandan (by-election 2025)
items.profile: PKR's most prominent second-generation reformist and now its deputy president; her Pandan victory over Rafizi consolidated the Anwar camp's grip on the party.

items.name: Saifuddin Nasution Ismail
items.role: Minister of Home Affairs; Secretary-General of Pakatan Harapan; Senator; PKR management committee advisor
items.seat: Senator (Dewan Negara; former MP Kulim-Bandar Baharu P018)
items.profile: PKR's chief administrator and PH's secretary-general; as Home Minister he has been a lightning rod for civil-liberties criticism but remains central to the government's machinery.

items.name: Amirudin Shari
items.role: 16th Menteri Besar of Selangor (2018–); PKR Vice-President; MP Gombak; PH Selangor chairman
items.profile: Two-term Selangor MB and the lynchpin of PKR's richest state; his state machinery is the party's GE16 electoral backbone.

items.name: Chang Lih Kang
items.role: Minister of Science, Technology & Innovation (2022–); PKR Vice-President; MP Tanjong Malim
items.profile: PKR's top ethnic-Chinese leader and MOSTI minister; a dependable technocrat whose Tanjong Malim seat is contested PH–BN territory in GE16.

items.name: Fahmi Fadzil
items.role: Minister of Communications (2023–); Government Spokesperson; PKR Information Chief; MP Lembah Pantai
items.profile: PH's chief communicator and a rare PKR figure who holds an urban mixed seat; central to the government's GE16 messaging.

items.name: Sim Tze Tzin
items.role: Deputy Minister of Investment, Trade & Industry (2025–); Political Secretary to the PKR President; MP Bayan Baru
items.profile: Penang-based PKR vice-presidential contender and policy workhorse; a bridge between PKR's reformist alumni and the current leadership.

items.name: William Leong Jee Keen
items.role: MP Selayang (2008–); Chair, Major Public Appointments Select Committee; PKR Treasurer-General
items.profile: A veteran PKR institutionalist who anchors the party's parliamentary oversight work; Selayang is a frontline seat against the PN surge.

items.name: Lee Chean Chung
items.role: MP Petaling Jaya (2022–); PKR Communications Director; Chair, Centre for Regional Strategic Studies
items.profile: PKR's urban policy face in the safest non-Malay-majority seat; represents the party's professional, reformist strand.

items.name: Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir
items.role: Minister of Economy (2025–); MP Johor Bahru; ex-PKR Youth Chief
items.profile: The youthful Economy Minister who inherited Rafizi's portfolio; his Johor Bahru seat is a key test of whether PKR's urban-Malay base holds.

items.name: Ramanan Ramakrishnan
items.role: Minister of Human Resources (2025–); PKR Vice-President; MP Sungai Buloh
items.profile: PKR's rising Tamil leader and HR minister; symbolises the party's multiracial ambitions in the Unity Government.

items.name: Anthony Loke Siew Fook
items.role: Secretary-General of DAP (2022–); Minister of Transport; MP Seremban
items.profile: DAP's de facto leader and a steady institutionalist; the Chennah defeat and his N9 resignation (Aug 2026) frame DAP's GE16 risk narrative.

items.name: Lim Guan Eng
items.role: DAP Advisor (2025–); former DAP National Chairman (2022–2025); MP Bagan; former Finance Minister
items.profile: The dominant DAP figure of the past two decades; now in an advisory role as the party renews its leadership around Loke and Gobind.

items.name: Lim Kit Siang
items.role: DAP founding-generation leader (retired); longest-serving Leader of the Opposition; MP for 8 terms
items.profile: The architect of the Malaysian Malaysia movement and DAP's founding father; retired but still the moral reference point of the party.

items.name: Gobind Singh Deo
items.role: National Chairman of DAP (2025–); Minister of Digital (2023–); MP Damansara
items.profile: DAP's National Chairman and Digital Minister; his rise to the chairmanship in 2025 marks the handover from the Lim generation to a new leadership core.

items.name: Teresa Kok Suh Sim
items.role: MP Seputeh (1999–); Deputy Chair, Public Accounts Committee (2024–); former Minister of Primary Industries
items.profile: DAP's most outspoken veteran and a fixture of Seputeh; her no-nonsense style keeps her a national headline-maker on religious-freedom and governance issues.

items.name: Hannah Yeoh Tseow Suan
items.role: Minister in the PM's Department (Federal Territories) (2025–); MP Segambut; DAP Deputy Secretary-General
items.profile: A flagship of DAP's generational renewal; her Federal Territories role gives KL voters direct cabinet representation ahead of GE16.

items.name: Nga Kor Ming
items.role: Minister of Housing & Local Government (2022–); Deputy National Chairman of DAP (2025–); MP Teluk Intan
items.profile: DAP's deputy chairman and a pugnacious Perak boss; a prolific ministry operator whose Teluk Intan seat is contested territory in GE16.

items.name: Chow Kon Yeow
items.role: 5th Chief Minister of Penang (2018–); MLA Padang Kota; MP Batu Kawan; PH Penang chairman
items.profile: The steady hand of Penang's DAP government for two terms; his state's strong fiscal record is PH's showcase in the north.

items.name: Steven Sim Chee Keong
items.role: Minister of Entrepreneur & Cooperatives Development (2025–); MP Bukit Mertajam; DAP Deputy Secretary-General; Penang DAP chairman
items.profile: A fast-rising DAP moderniser running two ministries in three years; a central figure in the party's Penang and national renewal.

items.name: Yeo Bee Yin
items.role: MP Puchong (2022–); DAP National Publicity Secretary; Selangor DAP secretary; Chair, PSC on Women, Children & Community Development
items.profile: DAP's clean-tech standard-bearer and a leading female voice; her technocratic profile is central to DAP's urban professional appeal.

items.name: Liew Chin Tong
items.role: Deputy Minister of Investment, Trade & Industry (2023–); MP Iskandar Puteri; MLA Perling; DAP National Strategic Director
items.profile: DAP's chief electoral strategist and a prolific political author; his Iskandar Puteri base anchors DAP's Johor push.

items.name: Teo Nie Ching
items.role: Deputy Minister of Communications (2023–); MP Kulai; DAP Women Chief; Johor DAP chair; DAP National Vice-Chairperson
items.profile: DAP's women's chief and Johor boss; a key operator in the southern state where PH is fighting the BN resurgence.

items.name: Tan Kok Wai
items.role: MP Cheras (1995–); longest-serving MP in the Dewan Rakyat; former DAP National Chairman; FT PH chairman
items.profile: The dean of the Dewan Rakyat and a DAP institutional pillar; his Cheras seat is among the party's safest.

items.name: M. Kulasegaran (Kula)
items.role: Deputy Minister in the PM's Department (Law & Institutional Reform) (2023–); MP Ipoh Barat (2004–)
items.profile: DAP's senior Indian-Malaysian leader and a champion of labour law; his graceful step-back from party polls signals DAP's leadership renewal.

items.name: Zairil Khir Johari
items.role: Penang EXCO member; MLA Tanjong Bunga; DAP Penang vice-chairman; former MP Bukit Bendera
items.profile: DAP's most prominent Malay leader and a Penang EXCO member; his presence counters the 'anti-Malay' narrative aimed at DAP.

items.name: Mohamad Sabu (Mat Sabu)
items.role: President of AMANAH (2015–); Minister of Agriculture & Food Security; MP Kota Raja
items.profile: AMANAH's founding president and moral anchor; the 'Mat Sabu' story — from ISA detainee to cabinet minister — embodies the progressive-Islam strand of PH.

items.name: Dr. Dzulkefly Ahmad
items.role: Minister of Health (2023–); AMANAH Vice-President; MP Kuala Selangor
items.profile: AMANAH's policy brain and two-time Health Minister; his scientific background anchors the party's technocratic-progressive identity.

items.name: Mujahid Yusof Rawa
items.role: Deputy President of AMANAH (2023–); Senator; Perak PH chairman; former Minister of Religious Affairs
items.profile: AMANAH's deputy president and a rare figure fluent in both Islamic and reformist discourses; bridges AMANAH's PAS heritage and PH's pluralism.

items.name: Mahfuz Omar
items.role: Vice-President of AMANAH (2021–); Chairman, Farmers' Organisation Authority (2023–); former MP Pokok Sena
items.seat: None (agency chairman; former MP Pokok Sena P008)
items.profile: AMANAH's Kedah veteran and a bridge between the party and the rural Malay base; his defection from PAS symbolised the 2018 opposition realignment.

items.name: Aminolhuda Hassan
items.role: AMANAH Johor chairman (2015–); MP Sri Gading; former Johor PH chairman; former Johor EXCO
items.profile: AMANAH's Johor boss and the MP for Sri Gading — a seat the base-case projection has flipping to BN on the Johor swing; a frontline GE16 incumbent.

items.name: Hasan Bahrom
items.role: Chairman, Yayasan Dakwah Islamiah Malaysia (YADIM) (2025–); former MP Tampin; AMANAH leader
items.profile: AMANAH's YADIM chairman and a former Tampin MP; represents the party's post-PAS institutional strand.

items.name: Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman
items.role: Founding President of MUDA; MP Muar; former Minister of Youth & Sports; Undi18 champion
items.profile: The face of Malaysia's youth-politics wave and MUDA's founder; his conviction, comeback and Muar seat make him the party's make-or-break figure for GE16.

items.name: Amira Aisya Abdul Aziz
items.role: Acting President / Deputy President of MUDA; former MLA Puteri Wangsa (2022–2026); co-founder
items.profile: MUDA's acting president and organisational backbone; her Puteri Wangsa defeat in Johor 2026 underscores the party's electoral fragility.

items.name: Amir Hariri Abdul Hadi
items.role: Co-founder; founding and 3rd Secretary-General of MUDA (2020–2021, 2022–2025)
items.profile: MUDA's chief organiser and a human-rights campaigner; the movement muscle behind the party's youth mobilisation.

items.name: Lim Wei Jiet
items.role: Co-founder of MUDA; constitutional lawyer; former party vice-president
items.profile: MUDA's founding lawyer whose courtroom work won the party its registration; the legal conscience of the youth-reform project.

items.name: Rafizi Ramli
items.role: De facto leader / co-founder of Bersama (2026–); former Minister of Economy (2022–2025); former PKR Deputy President; ex-MP Pandan
items.profile: The most consequential PKR defector of the decade; his Bersama splinter directly targets PKR's urban-Malay base and is the biggest internal threat to PH's GE16 arithmetic.

items.name: Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad
items.role: Deputy de facto leader / co-founder of Bersama (2026–); former Minister of Natural Resources & Environmental Sustainability; ex-MP Setiawangsa
items.profile: Rafizi's closest ally and Bersama's number two; his resignation from cabinet and Setiawangsa's vacancy marked the formal rupture of PKR's reformist wing.

items.name: Ahmad Syukri Che Abdul Razab
items.role: President of Parti Bersama Malaysia (nominal head)
items.profile: The nominal president of Bersama; a low-profile figurehead who enabled the Rafizi–Nik Nazmi relaunch.

items.name: Matthew Lai Jun-Loong
items.role: Vice-President of Parti Bersama Malaysia
items.profile: A member of Bersama's founding leadership slate; part of the party's bid to project a young, inclusive third force.

items.name: Abdul Hadi Awang
items.role: PAS President (since 2002); MP Marang (P037); former Terengganu MB (1999-2004)
items.profile: PAS's supreme leader and Malaysia's longest-serving party president; the anchor of the Malay-Muslim 'Green Wave' and the broker of PN's 2026 pro-PAS restructuring.

items.name: Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar
items.role: PN Chairman (2026); 15th Menteri Besar of Terengganu (since 2018); MP Kemaman (P040); PAS Vice President
items.seat: P040 Kemaman (MP since Dec 2023 by-election); Ru Rendang state seat, Terengganu (since 2018)

items.name: Takiyuddin Hassan
items.role: PAS Secretary-General (since 2015); PN Secretary-General (2026); MP Kota Bharu (P021)

items.name: Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor

items.profile: Kelantan's MB and a veteran of the state's PAS machine - keeper of PAS's longest-governed state ahead of GE16.
